messages.author: bc4bc847c10f529f
messages.subject: long compute time for plmData() on 12 MoGene-1_0-st-v1 arrays
parts:
Hi all,

I just did a doEverything() call (code by Mark Robinson, thanks very
much). I have 12 Mouse ST arrays. The call took 3.76 hrs, nearly
all of this time was due to the fit(plm) step (plm is the output from
RmaPlm). Does that seem like a usual length of time to anyone?

Total time for all units across all 12 arrays: 13522.67s == 225.38min
Total time per unit across all 12 arrays: 0.38s/unit
Total time per unit and array: 31.7ms/unit & array
Total time for one array (35512 units): 18.78min = 0.31h
Total time for complete data set: 225.38min = 3.76h
Fraction of time spent on different tasks: Fitting: 99.3%, Reading:
0.1%, Writing: 0.6% (of which 75.19% is for encoding/writing chip-
effects), Explicit garbage collection: 0.0%


Here is the version of doEverything:

doEverything<-function(name,chip,checkChipType=FALSE,

doExon=FALSE,doCore=FALSE,force=FALSE,doMerge=FALSE,doResiduals=FALSE,
doWeights=FALSE,getExpression=FALSE,verbose=Arguments$getVerbose(-8))
{

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chip,
checkChipType=checkChipType)
if (doCore)
chip<-paste(chip,",core",sep="")
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chip)
setCdf(cs, cdf)
bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs)
csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose,force=force)
setCdf(csBC, cdf)
qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose,force=force) #time required
setCdf(csN, cdf)
if (doExon)
plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csN,mergeGroups=doMerge)
else
plm <- RmaPlm(csN)
fit(plm, verbose=verbose,units=NULL) #time required
qam <- QualityAssessmentModel(plm)
chp<-getChipEffectSet(plm)
d<-NULL; ws<-NULL; rs<-NULL
if (getExpression) {
if (!doExon | doMerge)
d<-getExprs(chp,doExon=F)
else
d<-getExprs(chp,doExon=T)
}
if (doResiduals)
rs<-calculateResiduals(plm,verbose=verbose,force=force)
if (doWeights)
ws<-calculateWeights(plm,verbose=verbose,force=force)

list(name=name,chip=chip,d=d,cs=csN,cdf=cdf,plm=plm,qam=qam,chp=chp,res=rs,wts=ws)
}

You don't specify exactly how you call doEverything(), and what chip
type you are using ( MoEx-1_0-st or MoGene-1_0-st-v1?) but this is
certainly due the issue that in the CDF used there are a few units
that have >1000 probes each, cf. thread 'Summerization Speed Under
Unix' starting July 17, 2007, cf.

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/browse_thread/thread/f58b942da77d48d6

In that case MoEx-1_0-st-v1 was used. You basically want to identify
and exclude those big units from the fit. There is currently no way
to do this with doEverything(). See also Section 'More efficient
model fitting with hundreds of variables' at

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/optimization-speed-file-space-ram

which also show some code that you can use to identify large units, or
the other way around, identify the set of reasonably-sized units.
Let's call the latter integer vector 'units', then you call:

fit(plm, units=units, verbose=verbose)

in order to just fit those.

Hope this helps

Henrik

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Re: long compute time for plmData() on 12 MoGene-1_0-st-v1 arrays
parts:
Hi Dick,
If you are running the Exon Array (my personal experience) with just
the core probesets, the running time is slow for just 12 arrays, but
perhaps not in the category that some of the posts Henrik refers to. I
ran recently on a machine with 16GB memory the plm to fit the gene-
level estimates for Mark's Ensembl genes (about 20,000) on 53 chips
and it took about 40 minutes (.10sec/array)
#20071210 23:19:45| Total time for all units across all 53 arrays:
2346.98s == 39
#.12min
#20071210 23:19:45| Total time per unit across all 53 arrays:
0.10s/unit
#20071210 23:19:45| Total time per unit and array: 1.85ms/unit &
array
#20071210 23:19:45| Total time for one array (23885 units):
0.74min = 0.01h
#20071210 23:19:45| Total time for complete data set: 39.12min =
0.65h
#20071210 23:19:45| Fraction of time spent on different tasks:
Fitting: 83.0%, Re
#ading: 9.4%, Writing: 7.4% (of which 79.43% is for encoding/
writing chip-effects
#), Explicit garbage collection: 0.2%
#20071210 23:19:45|Fitting model of class ExonRmaPlm:...done
Fitting to the exons (merge=F) took less time (30 minutes); residuals
were very fast (<10minutes!) and weights were about 40minues. I don't
have the time on the earlier steps (bg and qn), but I would guess that
the overall time was between 2 and 3 hours. But this was a very fast
machine. I have run on my home machine (for the core probesets) and
certain steps (e.g. residuals) took much longer because the memory was
low. For the fitting, for plm fitting of the exons (merge=F) it took
an hour instead of 30 minutes for the same set of arrays; I no longer
have the output for my home machine on the gene-level fitting, but I
think it's generally longer because of the bigger sets of probes given
to the fitting.

If you are running off of Affymetrix's default chip, you probably
shouldn't! Unless you are really interested in mRNAs that don't map to
the genome, use one of the probesets I made available
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/affymetrix-defined-transcript-clusters
You can still get probeset summaries by choosing mergeGroups=FALSE.
Affy's has these ridiculously long probesets (10,000+ probes) that are
not part of the exon design but various gridding probes and other
controls. Those are the ones referred to in the post Henrik linked to.
In addition it's not binary, so if you didn't convert it, it would be
very slow reading it.

Best,
Elizabeth

Some time ago I "took measure" to prevent that problem:

Version: 0.6.2 [2007-09-07]
o Now setCdf() of AffymetrixCelSet throws an (informative) error message
whenever one tries to use an ASCII CDF file. This behavior can be
changed by setting rule 'aroma.affymetrix.settings$rules$allowAsciiCdfs'
to TRUE in the options. The reason is that working with ASCII CDF files
is extremely slow and memory inefficient. Use affxparser::convertCdf()
to convert a CDF into a binary format.

setCdf() is called internally when setting up a CEL set, so
aroma.affymetrix will given an error when you load the data (unless
you change the settings which is more complicated than creating the
binary CDF).

Cheers

Henrik

I don't think it would be a hard thing at all, though it takes a while
and a lot of memory to make all of them (on berkeley servers, they
take about a week to create all 4 of them, but the smaller ones are
done in a day or two). I have code that takes as input the NetAffx
data (or other similar file with one entry per *probeset*) and
converts the default Affy cdf into one with the nested exon/gene
structure. In fact, my current version is in aroma.affymetrix.tools
that you set up for Mark and I to put trial functions in -- and Mark
has used it successfully, so that's good. Can anyone source a function
in from there?
Best,
Elizabeth

On Dec 13, 2007 8:41 AM, Henrik Bengtsson <h...@stat.berkeley.edu > wrote:

> all of this time was due to the fit(plm) step (plm is the output from
> RmaPlm).  Does that seem like a usual length of time to anyone?

You don't specify exactly how you call doEverything(), and what chip
type you are using ( MoEx-1_0-st or MoGene-1_0-st-v1?) but this is
certainly due the issue that in the CDF used there are a few units
that have >1000 probes each, cf. thread 'Summerization Speed Under
Unix' starting July 17, 2007, cf.

 http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/browse_thread/thread/f58b942da77d48d6

In that case MoEx-1_0-st-v1 was used.  You basically want to identify
and exclude those big units from the fit.  There is currently no way
to do this with doEverything().  See also Section 'More efficient
model fitting with hundreds of variables' at

 http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/optimization-speed-file-space-ram

which also show some code that you can use to identify large units, or
the other way around, identify the set of reasonably-sized units.
Let's call the latter integer vector 'units', then you call:

 fit(plm, units=units, verbose=verbose)

in order to just fit those.

Hope this helps

Henrik
